title: PRILOSEC (omeprazole magnesium) granule, delayed release: full prescribing information
authors: Covis Pharma US, Inc.; approved by the US Food and Drug Administration
journal: US Food and Drug Administration-approved labelling, published in DailyMed (National Library of Medicine); structured product label version 8, effective 19 March 2024; initial US approval 1989
funder: not stated; FDA-approved labelling carries no funding statement
result: No boxed warning. Warnings and precautions 5.1 to 5.13: symptomatic response does not preclude gastric malignancy; acute tubulointerstitial nephritis may occur at any point during therapy, sometimes without extra-renal signs, and requires discontinuation; Clostridium difficile-associated diarrhoea, especially in hospitalised patients; osteoporosis-related fractures of hip, wrist or spine with high-dose (multiple daily doses) and long-term (a year or longer) therapy; severe cutaneous adverse reactions including Stevens-Johnson syndrome, toxic epidermal necrolysis, DRESS and AGEP; cutaneous and systemic lupus erythematosus, new or exacerbated, within weeks to years of continuous therapy, most patients improving 4 to 12 weeks after stopping; avoid clopidogrel; daily acid suppression longer than about 3 years may cause cyanocobalamin malabsorption; hypomagnesaemia reported rarely after at least 3 months and in most cases after a year, with tetany, arrhythmias and seizures, possibly causing hypocalcaemia or hypokalaemia, in most patients requiring magnesium replacement and discontinuation; chromogranin A rises and gives false-positive neuroendocrine tumour tests (stop at least 14 days before testing); high-dose methotrexate toxicity; fundic gland polyps with risk rising with use beyond one year. Contraindicated with rilpivirine; hypersensitivity may include anaphylaxis, angioedema, bronchospasm and acute tubulointerstitial nephritis. Warfarin co-use raised INR, which may lead to abnormal bleeding and death. Postmarketing reports include pancreatitis, hepatic failure, agranulocytosis and SJS/TEN (each some fatal), microscopic colitis, hyponatraemia, hypoglycaemia and optic neuropathies. Serum gastrin rose in the first 1 to 2 weeks, median 1.3- to 3.6-fold with omeprazole 20 mg against 1.1- to 1.8-fold with H2-receptor antagonists, and returned to baseline 1 to 2 weeks after stopping; gastrin causes ECL-cell hyperplasia and chromogranin A rise. In biopsies from more than 3000 patients in long-term trials, ECL-cell hyperplasia increased with time without carcinoid, dysplasia or neoplasia, but the studies were of insufficient duration and size to rule out an influence on premalignant or malignant conditions. Omeprazole for 14 days raised intragastric viable bacteria, resolving within 3 days of stopping. In two 24-month rat studies at 1.7 to 140.8 mg/kg/day (about 0.4 to 34 times a 40 mg human dose by body surface area), omeprazole produced dose-related gastric ECL-cell carcinoids, more in females; ECL-cell hyperplasia occurred in all treated groups. Esomeprazole reduced femur weight and length in juvenile rats. Erosive oesophagitis healing at 8 weeks: 74% with 20 mg (n = 83), 75% with 40 mg (n = 87), 14% with placebo (n = 43); endoscopic remission at 6 months: 70% with 20 mg daily (n = 138) against 11% with placebo (n = 131). Efficacy beyond 8 weeks for erosive oesophagitis is not established; controlled maintenance studies do not extend beyond 12 months.
